THE DESK'S TOP 5 HIGHEST-CONVICTION TRADES FOR TODAY -- 2026-07-22 This is the unconstrained slot on the desk. No candidate pool, no sector limit, no asset-class restriction -- stocks, commodities, ETFs, crypto, or a flat WAIT are all fair game, and the only rule is that the five ideas cannot collapse into five versions of the same trade. Context for today: Brent crude $94.42 (+3.8%), Gold $4119.50 (+1.1%), 10Y yield 4.6%, VIX 18.6. The dominant macro driver right now is the Strait of Hormuz standoff -- Iran has declared the strait closed following the collapse of a preliminary US-Iran ceasefire, commercial crude inventories are running roughly 6% below the five-year seasonal average (per EIA data through the week of July 10), and diesel crack spreads are at records -- a setup where low starting inventories make any further disruption disproportionately price-sensitive, even though the IEA's longer-run view still points to a 3.7-4.0mb/d oversupply once the geopolitical premium fades. The second live macro thread is China's rare-earth and graphite export-control overhang: the IEA flagged on July 16 that full implementation could put $6.5 trillion of downstream Western production at risk, with the expanded controls currently suspended only until November 2026 -- a live, dated trigger, not a vague worry. #1 -- MP MATERIALS (MP) -- COMMODITY MINER -- Conviction: HIGH The single best idea on the desk today. MP is the only rare-earth mining-and-processing operation of scale in North America, sitting directly in the crosshairs of the China export-control deadline (controls suspended only until November 2026) that the IEA just re-flagged as a $6.5 trillion downstream risk. What makes this asymmetric rather than just a geopolitical bet is the government backstop: MP has a Department of Defense partnership (with pricing-floor-style support) and a long-term supply agreement with Apple, which puts a soft floor under the downside even as the stock has pulled back roughly 15% over the past 30 days on near-term China-risk jitters (Barclays trimmed its target to $65 on July 15, while Deutsche Bank raised its target to $70 the same week -- a split-analyst tape that usually means the market hasn't settled on a narrative yet, which is exactly when I want to be positioned). FMP-verified financials (fetched directly): FY2025 revenue of $275.5mn, up 35% from $203.9mn in FY2024, still net-loss-making (-$85.9mn) but sitting on $1.17bn of cash against $1.04bn of debt (net cash position), reflecting the capital MP has raised on the back of the DoD deal -- a balance sheet built for the fight, not a distressed one. Consensus price target on FMP data is $80.70 (range $69-$100) against a recent price near $54-55, real upside even before crediting any near-term supply-disruption premium. This rests on judgment, not a screen: no mechanical value or momentum screen would flag a loss-making miner with a stock down 15% in a month -- the case is entirely about reading the geopolitical calendar (November 2026 China deadline) and the government-backstop structure correctly. Distinct from the other four: this is the only idea driven by a specific critical-minerals supply-chain policy calendar, and the only one where a government counterparty effectively underwrites downside. #2 -- ALPHABET (GOOGL) -- CATALYST-DRIVEN STOCK -- Conviction: HIGH Alphabet reports earnings TODAY, July 22, 2026 -- a binary, same-day catalyst, which is the whole reason this slot exists. The swing factor the whole market is watching is AI capital-expenditure guidance: after a run of aggressive capex increases across the hyperscalers, any signal that Alphabet is either decelerating spend (read by the market as fear of an AI-capex bubble popping) or reaccelerating it (read as confidence, but also as margin-dilutive in the near term) will move the stock and the broader AI-infrastructure trade hard in either direction within hours of the print. FMP-verified financials (fetched directly) show why the stakes are high: FY2025 revenue of $402.96bn, up 15.1% from $350.02bn in FY2024, net income up to $132.17bn from $100.12bn, and a consensus price target of $420.14 (range $360-$460) -- a company executing extremely well on the current model, which is precisely why a capex-guidance surprise in either direction, not the trailing numbers, is what moves the stock today. This is a same-day, binary, watch-the-tape trade, not a multi-year thesis -- and it rests on judgment (which side of the "capex fear vs. capex confidence" reaction function the market is currently primed for, based on how the last two hyperscaler prints were received) rather than anything a screen would output, since screens don't have a view on tonight's earnings call tone. Distinct from the other four: this is the only idea where the catalyst fires today with certainty (the print exists on the calendar no matter what), versus the geopolitically-contingent or macro-drift catalysts elsewhere on this list. #3 -- ENERGY SELECT SECTOR SPDR (XLE) -- MACRO/ETF PLAY -- Conviction: MEDIUM-HIGH With Brent up 3.8% to $94.42 on Strait-of-Hormuz closure risk and diesel crack spreads at records, the cleanest way to express "this geopolitical premium persists longer than consensus expects" without taking single-name E&amp;P or refiner risk is the broad energy-equities complex via XLE. The case for staying long here rather than fading the spike: EIA data through the week of July 10 shows commercial crude inventories running roughly 6% below the five-year seasonal average, which means the market has very little buffer left to absorb an actual disruption -- if Iran's declared closure of the strait produces even a partial, temporary interruption to the roughly one-fifth of global oil consumption that transits it, the low-inventory starting point amplifies the price reaction well beyond a "normal" supply headline. I hold this alongside, not instead of, the IEA's longer-term 3.7-4.0mb/d oversupply call -- that's a 2027+ story; the next two to three months are about inventory tightness and geopolitical premium, which is squarely XLE's holding period. This is a macro/positioning call, not a name-specific pick, and it's an explicit judgment that the current premium has more room before it fades, which is inherently a view a screen cannot generate (screens report today's price, not tomorrow's Hormuz headline risk). Distinct from the other four: this is a sector-broad, macro-driven ETF expression of a geopolitical event, deliberately avoiding single-name miner risk (that's slot #1) and crypto/rotation risk (that's slot #5). #4 -- NIKE (NKE) -- CONTRARIAN PICK -- Conviction: MEDIUM Nike is down roughly 33-43% from its highs over the trailing year and looks, on the surface, like a broken story -- but the turnaround under CEO Elliott Hill's "Sport Offense" strategy just produced a genuinely startling data point: EPS of $0.72 against a Street estimate of $0.13, a beat of well over 400%. FMP-verified financials (fetched directly) show FY2026 (ended May 31, 2026) revenue of $46.40bn, essentially flat year-over-year against FY2025's $46.31bn but still well below FY2024's $51.36bn -- so the top line hasn't recovered, but the fact that profitability is inflecting this hard on a flat top line is the actual signal, not the still-depressed revenue base. What moves this from "value trap" to "contrarian buy" for me is the insider tape, visible directly in FMP's insider-trading feed: CEO Elliott Hill personally bought roughly 23,660 shares around $42.27 in April 2026, and board member Timothy D. Cook (yes, Apple's CEO, who sits on Nike's board) bought 25,000 shares at $42.43 the same week -- open-market purchases by the people with the best visibility into whether the turnaround is real, at prices close to where the stock still trades. Consensus price target of $51.28 (FMP data, range $35-$75) sits meaningfully above the insider entry price, and well above where the stock was trading through the depths of the selloff. This is a contrarian call precisely because the sell-side spread (high target $75, low target $35) shows the Street itself hasn't agreed on the story yet -- which is usually where the better risk/reward sits, not after consensus has already formed. Distinct from the other four: this is the only idea built on a company-specific turnaround-plus-insider-buying signal in a beaten-down consumer name, unrelated to today's commodity, macro, or tech-earnings catalysts. #5 -- BITCOIN (BTC) -- CRYPTO / SECTOR ROTATION -- Conviction: MEDIUM (tactical, smaller size) Bitcoin bled roughly 20% through June, touching the low-$60,000s and briefly dipping under $60,000 -- its worst level in over 21 months -- as sticky rates, a firmer dollar, and intense competition for risk capital from AI-related equities sapped the bid, before stabilizing back into the $60,000-$65,000 zone in recent sessions. The tactical case for a rotation trade here rather than a "buy the dip and forget it" call: July has historically been one of Bitcoin's stronger seasonal months (green in 9 of the last 13 years, average return north of 7%), and if the current level holds as support rather than breaking down further, the historical pattern is for capital to then rotate down the risk curve into altcoins tied to live narratives -- AI-compute and DePIN tokens, and majors like Solana, Chainlink and XRP, have shown relative resilience even as the broader tape stayed soft. I am sizing this as the smallest of the five ideas and framing it explicitly as tactical rather than core, because the macro backdrop working against crypto (sticky rates, strong dollar, AI-equity competition for the same risk dollars) hasn't actually changed -- I am betting on a seasonal mean-reversion pattern holding one more year, which is a real edge if the pattern holds and a real loss if a fresh leg down through $58k breaks the seasonal precedent. This is unambiguously a judgment call, not a screen output -- there is no fundamental valuation model that produces a "buy Bitcoin here" signal; the entire case rests on reading price-seasonality and cross-asset risk-appetite rotation correctly. Distinct from the other four: this is the only idea outside traditional equities/commodities entirely, and the only one explicitly flagged as tactical/smaller-size rather than a full-conviction core position -- it exists to satisfy genuine thesis diversity, not to force a fifth stock pick into the slot. Why this is five distinct trades, not five correlated tech or commodity bets: #1 is a single-name critical-minerals miner with a government-backstop catalyst; #2 is a same-day binary mega-cap-tech earnings event; #3 is a sector-broad macro/geopolitical ETF expression; #4 is a beaten-down consumer-discretionary turnaround driven by insider buying; #5 is a tactical crypto-seasonality rotation call sized smaller than the other four. None of these ideas share a catalyst, a sector, or an asset class, by design.

Three simultaneously live geopolitical fronts (active US-Iran war disrupting Hormuz shipping, a fragile and still-unresolved Russia-Ukraine conflict, and elevated but non-military Taiwan Strait tension) plus a tariff-authority cliff (Section 122 expiring July 24) is an unusually dense cluster of tail risks for a VIX still sitting at only 18.6 — that gap between headline risk and priced volatility is itself the elevated-crash-risk signal, not any single scenario being the base case.

AI MARKET SYNOPSIS

Broad screen surfaced 15 candidates across enterprise software, EM fintech, semicap/dicing equipment, and Nordic industrials; the desk converged on a real BUY/WATCH/AVOID/KILL spread (3 BUY, 8 WATCH, 3 AVOID/KILL) rather than rubber-stamping the initial theses, with Halozyme, H&R Block, and Adobe emerging as the highest-conviction ideas after full verification and debate.

🌍 GEOPOLITICAL & MACRO CONTEXT

The dominant macro story right now is an active, multi-week US-Iran military conflict disrupting Strait of Hormuz shipping (Brent $94.42, +3.75%, and gold $4,119.5, +1.06%, per FMP cross_asset directly reflect this), layered on top of a US tariff-authority cliff (Section 122 expires July 24, with the administration rebuilding via Sections 301/232 and fresh Canada/Mexico tariff threats), a still-unresolved Russia-Ukraine war where peace talks continue but ceasefires keep breaking down, and elevated-but-non-military Taiwan Strait tension driving TSMC's accelerated US capex shift. Despite this unusually dense cluster of geopolitical risk, the yield curve has re-steepened to +0.37 and VIX sits at a moderate 18.6 — markets currently appear to be treating these as contained/regional risks rather than systemic ones, which is itself worth watching given how quickly any one of the three live conflicts could re-escalate.
